llm.answer:
**Core Graphics – Apple Developer Documentation (PDF)** *(All information is drawn from the three uploaded pages of the same PDF.)* | Section | Key Points | Source | |---------|------------|--------| | **Framework Overview** | • Core Graphics is a low‑level, lightweight 2‑D rendering engine built on Quartz.
• It delivers unmatched output fidelity and is used for path‑based drawing, transformations, color management, off‑screen rendering, patterns, gradients, shading, image data handling, image creation, image masking, PDF creation, display, and parsing.
• On macOS it also exposes services for display‑hardware control, low‑level user‑input events, and the windowing system. | [Source 1] | | **Supported Platforms & Languages** | • iOS 2.0+, iPadOS 2.0+, Mac Catalyst 13.1+, macOS 10.8+, tvOS 9.0+, visionOS 1.0+, watchOS 2.0+.
• Primary language: Swift (but also available in Objective‑C). | [Source 1] | | **Core Data Types** | • `CGFloat` – basic floating‑point scalar.
• `CGPoint`, `CGSize`, `CGRect` – geometric primitives for points, sizes, and rectangles. | [Source 1] | | **Primary Structures & Classes** | • **Geometry & Transformations** – `CGVector`, `CGAffineTransform`.
• **Drawing Context** – `CGContext` (Quartz 2D drawing environment).
• **Images & Paths** – `CGImage`, `CGImageMask`, `CGPath`, `CGMutablePath`.
• **Layers & Colors** – `CGLayer`, `CGColor`, `CGColorSpace`, `CGColorConversionInfo`.
• **Fonts & Text** – `CGFont`.
• **PDF Support** – `CGPDFDocument`.
• **Data I/O** – `CGDataConsumer`, `CGDataProvider`.
• **Gradients & Shading** – `CGGradient`, `CGShading`.
• **Functions & Patterns** – `CGFunction`, `CGPattern`. | [Source 1] | | **PDF‑Specific Types** | • `CGPDFMarkedContentItem`, `CGPDFStructureElement`. | [Source 3] | | **Rendering & Buffering** | • `CGRenderingBufferProvider` – abstraction for rendering buffers.
• `CGBitmapParameters` – bitmap configuration. | [Source 3] | | **Color & Image Enums** | • `CGBitmapLayout`, `CGComponent`, `CGContentToneMappingInfo`, `CGImageComponentInfo`. | [Source 3] | | **Quartz Services** | • **Display Services** – direct access to macOS window server for display‑hardware configuration.
• **Event Services** – manage event taps (filters for observing/altering low‑level user‑input streams).
• **Window Services** – information about windows managed by the macOS window server. | [Source 1] | | **Utility & Support** | • A collection of helper classes, structures, enumerations, constants, and functions that support the framework’s core capabilities. | [Source 1] | | **Documentation & Guides** | • “Quartz 2D Programming Guide” and related Apple documentation pages are referenced for deeper dives. | [Source 1] | ### Take‑away Summary Core Graphics is the foundational 2‑D rendering engine on Apple platforms, providing a rich set of low‑level APIs for drawing, image manipulation, PDF handling, and color management. It exposes a comprehensive suite of geometric types, drawing contexts, image and path objects, and PDF‑specific structures, all built atop the Quartz engine. Additional services allow developers to tap into display hardware, handle low‑level input events, and manage window information on macOS. The framework is cross‑platform (iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS) and is primarily used via Swift (though Objective‑C bindings exist).
